event: Elsie wakes to the bread smell, with Tamsin's knuckle wrap on the sill beside Sunny.
Through the Tether she feels Tamsin somewhere across town: a sore, warm ache in one forearm.
She opens her window by wishing and reads the new word under Tether: Hold.
She says it aloud twice, once like a gaoler and once like a hug, and settles on the hug.
She waters the plants and tells Mrs Pennywhistle the fern that she has levelled up.
Downstairs the baker sets out a honey bun for her unasked, and Elsie pays for it.
Elsie asks if the honey cake in the window has a recipe; the baker says it lives in her hands.
Elsie says Tamsin's mother loves honey cake, and asks if she might learn it one day.
The baker looks at her a long moment and says: tonight, after closing, bring the firewood money.
At the guild hall heads turn as Elsie comes in, and the talk drops to whispers.
Two swordsmen at the board say Enthraller, and Tether, and Berserker, and stare at her.
Tamsin shoulders through the door with her forearm bandaged, and grins at Elsie across the hall.
Elsie checks the bandage at once, and Tamsin lets her, standing very still.
Tamsin says she slept the whole night through, the first time in a year, and can't say why.
Tilly arrives at a run with a pear fizz for each of them, and they drink them at the board.
Elsie wipes soot off Tilly's cheek with her thumb, and Tilly forgets what she was saying.
Cora comes out of the charcoal door and says the guildmaster wants Elsie upstairs, with Tamsin.
Elsie buys Cora a black tea with one sugar at the hall counter and hands it to her.
Cora takes it without a word, and drinks it on the stairs.
Tilly waits by the board while Elsie, Tamsin and Cora go up to the guildmaster's office.
The guildmaster has grey hair and a sword on the wall, and asks Cora for the ledger.
She reads the Glasswood page and asks Tamsin if she gave her leave.
Tamsin says yes, before the guild, and she would give it again right now.
The guildmaster asks Elsie what the Tether does, and Elsie tells her plainly, the ache too.
Elsie says Tamsin may break it whenever she likes; Tamsin says she likes it where it is.
The guildmaster says the Tether stands, and Cora goes on writing every line.
She asks if Elsie knows what the city will say; Elsie says she hopes it says Tamsin is safe.
Back downstairs Tilly waits by the Leftovers, and so do three of the Copper Hounds.
Their leader says the Hounds will take Tamsin back, now that she is on a leash.
Tamsin's grin goes; Elsie steps in front of her before she can answer.
Elsie says it is no leash, it is Tamsin's, and Tamsin chooses.
Tamsin puts a hand on Elsie's shoulder and says her name is chalked on a slate already.
The Hounds' leader looks at Elsie a long while and goes back to her table.
Tamsin keeps her hand on Elsie's shoulder the whole length of the board.
New notices are up on the F-rank board: a lost cat, a flower cart escort, glowcaps underground.
Tilly says glowcaps mean underground, very quietly, and Elsie squeezes her hand.
Elsie picks the lost cat on the rooftops of Tanner's Row; Tamsin says she can climb anything.
The clerk enters the party for the cat, and Cora writes it in her ledger.
Tanner's Row smells of leather, and its roofs lean close across a narrow lane.
An old woman in a doorway says the cat is Pudding, ginger, and he will not come down.
She says Pudding has been up there two days and hisses at the ladder man.
Tamsin goes up a drainpipe to the first roof, and Pudding watches her from a chimney.
Pudding spits at Tamsin and climbs to the next roof up.
Tilly mixes a fishy paste in her palm, apologising for the smell the whole time.
Elsie climbs the ladder with the paste on a rag, and Tamsin hauls her up by both wrists.
On the roof Tamsin keeps hold of her wrists a while, and says the slates are slippery.
Cora calls up from the lane that she is staying where the ground is, and watches.
Pudding sits on the ridge and looks at Elsie with flat yellow eyes.
Tamsin asks if Elsie can't just Captivate him down.
Elsie says the cat hasn't agreed, and she wouldn't anyway; she sits down on the slates.
Below, Cora stops with her pen above the ledger, then writes.
Elsie holds out the rag and tells Pudding about her plants, humming in between.
Pudding comes down the ridge a step at a time and climbs into Elsie's lap.
He purrs, and Tamsin sits close behind Elsie on the slates to steady her.
Tamsin's chin is by Elsie's shoulder, and Elsie leans back into her without thinking.
Something warm and quick comes down the Tether from Tamsin; Elsie puts it down to the height.
They climb down; Tamsin goes first and catches Elsie off the last rung, cat and all.
The old woman cries over Pudding and gives them each a sugared bun, eaten in the lane.
Tilly picks ginger hairs off Elsie's skirt one by one, carefully, and goes pink.
At the Tipsy Heron Tamsin pays for stew for herself, Elsie and Tilly, and Cora pays for her own.
Tilly asks Tamsin if the sleeping is the Tether; Elsie says she honestly doesn't know.
Cora says she will write it down if it happens again.
Under the tavern noise Tilly asks Elsie if a Tether can hold two people.
Elsie says she supposes so, if the other one wanted it; Tilly goes scarlet into her stew.
At the guild hall the clerk pays the cat notice, and Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly each pocket a third.
Cora says she has her report to write, and goes in at the charcoal door.
Tamsin says her mother's barge ties up on the Long Cut tomorrow, and asks Elsie to meet her.
Elsie says yes before she has finished, and says she will bring honey cake.
Tamsin laughs and says she never told her that; Elsie says she did, and wrote it down.
Tamsin stops laughing and looks at Elsie as if something hit her.
Tilly says she has a brew to finish and goes, then runs back to hug Elsie, then goes.
Tamsin walks Elsie home along Thimble Canal with Margery on her shoulder.
At the Honeycomb door Tamsin says tomorrow, early, and goes off whistling.
In the attic Elsie writes: Tamsin's mother, the barge, the Long Cut, honey cake.
She sleeps an hour with the round window open and the canal sounds coming in.
At closing she comes down with the firewood money, and the baker ties an apron on her.
The baker sets a whole comb of honey on the table; Elsie pays for that too, and the baker lets her.
The baker says nothing is written down, so watch; Elsie watches every move.
She melts the comb slowly while Elsie stirs and hums, and the baker says hum less.
Elsie writes each step in her notebook in a floury pencil, and the baker reads over her shoulder.
The baker says her own mother taught her, and she has never taught anyone since.
The cake comes out golden; the baker covers it with a cloth and says it must rest a night.
Elsie asks why; the baker says some things are better for waiting.
Elsie washes every bowl while the baker sits on a stool and watches her.
Upstairs Elsie feels Tamsin down the Tether, settled and warm, somewhere across town.
She writes her weekly letter to her mother: a cat, a cake, and a girl who sleeps now.
She lays out a clean cloth and her best ribbon for the cake, and goes to bed early.
